name: Punctured-Cube Protection Equals Complementary Root Locking
statement: For a nested ample pair $A\subsetneq B$, the following are equivalent: the pair is upper-root-locked; every $x\in B\setminus A$ lies in the interior $\mathsf I(y,S)$ of an absent-tip punctured cube $\mathsf P(y,S)\subseteq B$ with $|S|\ge2$; and, in the rooted signed presentation of the complementary pair, every relative vertex remains joined to the root after deleting all coordinate labels incident with that vertex at the root. Moreover, if $x=y^T$ is protected by such a block, every one-coordinate neighbour $x^{\{q\}}$ with $q\in T$ lies in $B$, so the block induces a root path avoiding all labels deleted by the complementary cut test.
proof: The canonical one-hole normal form identifies upper-root-locking with punctured-cube protection, while the rooted relative presentation identifies upper-root-locking with the complementary labelled cut condition. For a protected word $x=y^T$, removing any $q\in T$ leaves a nonempty subset of the punctured-cube support, so $x^{\{q\}}\in B$. Thus no coordinate of $T$ is removed in the complementary cut test, and the root-cut criterion converts the missing-tip relation into the stated surviving path.
